# Add state-aware affordability filtering for storyline options

## Summary

Extend `getStorylineOptions` (or add a companion state-aware accessor) that filters out unaffordable options based on `cost` fields. Store the presented/available option list on `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Affordability filter.** `getAffordableOptions(state, event)` returns options where `cost` is affordable (coins and/or reputation gates checked). Options with no cost are always included.
- **Pending choice stores presented list.** `PendingEventChoice` gains an optional `presentedOptions: StorylineOption[]` field populated at choice-draw time.
- **Filtering is stable.** The presented list is computed once at draw and does not change during the pending choice period.
- **Backwards compatible.** Events with no cost-gated options return the same list as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `getAffordableOptions()`, update `createPendingStorylineChoice()` to populate `presentedOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `presentedOptions` to `PendingEventChoice`.

## Deliverables

- New/pure function `getAffordableOptions`.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice` populates `presentedOptions`.
- Unit tests for affordability filter.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — deterministic filtering.

# Deduct cost and apply extra effects during storyline option resolution

## Summary

At resolution time (`resolveStorylineOption` / `resolveEventOption`), deduct the option's `cost` from the player's resources and apply any `extraEffect` independently of the `effectPolicy`. This is the core gameplay change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost deduction.** When an affordable option is selected, its `cost.coins` (if set) and `cost.reputation` (if set) are deducted from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effect application.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`. Both can coexist (e.g. accept + pay cost + apply extra).
- **Log messages.** Activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Loss checks.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `cost` or `extraEffect` behave identically to pre-change.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `resolveStorylineOption` applies cost + extra effect.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` logging updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveStorylineOption` and `resolveEventOption`.
- Updated log messages.
- Unit tests for cost/extra effect application.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — straightforward resource mutation.

# Resolve conditional successors at option resolution time

## Summary

When resolving an option, evaluate `conditionalSuccessors` in order — the first matching rule wins. Fall back to the option's existing `successorId` when no conditions match. This enables branching based on game state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Conditional evaluation.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule whose `{ field, op, value }` matches current `state.resourceBank.{field}` determines the pushed card ID.
- **Fallback.** When no conditions match, the option's `successorId` is used.
- **All boundary cases tested.** Above/below threshold, equality boundary (`==`), and no-match fallback.
- **Successor-card push.** The matched successor is pushed via `pushChainCard` as before.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `conditionalSuccessors` push `successorId` as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Update `resolveStorylineOption` to evaluate conditional successors.

## Deliverables

- Conditional successor evaluation logic.
- Unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNYFJT006PKLC (cost deduction and extra effects).
- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — pure predicate evaluation.

# Update resolveEventOption to use the stored presented option list

## Summary

`resolveEventOption` in `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` currently indexes into `getStorylineOptions(event)` (the full list). Update it to use `pending.presentedOptions` (the affordability-filtered list) so the option index stored at draw time maps correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Index into presented list.** `resolveEventOption` resolves using `pending.presentedOptions[optionIndex]` instead of `getStorylineOptions(event)[optionIndex]`.
- **Fallback to full list.** When `presentedOptions` is null/empty, fall back to `getStorylineOptions(event)`.
- **Transcript stability.** The transcript records the chosen option label from the presented list.
- **Backwards compatible.** Legacy events without `presentedOptions` behave identically.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses `pending.presentedOptions`.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveEventOption`.
- Unit tests confirming index stability.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed.

# Update AI policy to select only among presented/affordable options

## Summary

`decideEventChoice` in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` currently returns `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`. Generalise it to select from the presented option list, accounting for cost and extra-effect deltas when projecting outcomes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AI selects from presented options.** The AI considers only options in the presented list (already filtered by affordability).
- **Cost-aware projection.** When projecting outcomes, the AI accounts for `cost` and `extraEffect` in addition to `effectPolicy` effects.
- **Regression harness passes.** The Monte Carlo and regression harnesses run to completion without AI stalls or invalid selections.
- **Backwards compatible.** For legacy binary-choice events, AI behaviour is identical to before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` generalised for multi-way affordability-aware selection.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolvePendingEventChoice` wiring updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated AI policy.
- Regression/Monte Carlo harness tests green.
- Unit tests for AI policy with cost-gated options.

Update the static validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) and the JSON schema (`schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`) to understand and validate the new optional fields. Reject invalid data (negative costs, unknown fields/ops, dangling conditional successors).

# Create a card shader

## Problem statement

Upgraded business / community-space cards (level > 0) are currently distinguished only by a flat golden stroke, a small `Lvl N` badge, and a baked display-name variant. These read as "a normal card with a border" rather than a visibly special, premium card. The seed asks for a **custom card shader** that can be applied to upgraded cards so they look distinct at a glance on a crowded street.

**Producer decisions (2026-10-09):**
- **Q1 = A** — implement a **Canvas-compatible shader-style effect now** using the existing overlay pipeline. A true GPU shader (WebGL Filters/custom shaders) is out of scope and deferred behind a separate low-priority renderer migration (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`).
- **Q2 = A** — scope is **upgraded business/community-space cards only** (level > 0).
- **Q3** — the existing **full-card golden `upgradeBorder` is being removed** by the player/AI identification work item `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`, which makes the owner colour the outer card border and moves the upgrade indicator to the top-left level badge / corner accent. This item must **not** depend on or recreate that full-card border; the shader effect is the upgrade distinction and must coexist with owner-coloured outer borders.
- **Q4 = as recommended** — the effect is **animated, with a reduced-motion static fallback**.
- **Q5 = default** — no regression to the existing suite; animation paused in replay/headless.

## Users

- **Main Street player (street overview)** — wants to spot upgraded businesses instantly when scanning the 2×5 street, including under competitive/owner-coloured rendering.
- **Main Street player (mid/late game)** — wants the payoff of investing in upgrades to feel visually rewarding, not just a stat change.
- **Main Street player with reduced motion enabled** — wants the same distinction in a static form.
- **Main Street developer** — wants the effect delivered through the existing upgrade overlay pipeline with a pure, testable spec builder and a Canvas-safe fallback.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want upgraded cards to carry a distinctive animated/premium treatment so that I can tell them apart from base cards without reading the level badge.
- As a Main Street player with reduced motion enabled, I want the same distinction in a static form so that the game stays comfortable to use.
- As a Main Street developer, I want the effect driven by a pure spec builder so that it can be unit-tested without a Phaser runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Upgraded business/community-space cards (level > 0) render a distinctive shader-style effect** (e.g. animated gradient/shimmer on the corner accent / inner glow) via the existing overlay pipeline, with **no change to the Phaser render type**; base cards (level 0) render unchanged.
2. The effect is driven by a **pure, Phaser-free spec** (extending `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` or a sibling pure module) so it is unit-testable, and the spec builder's base-card output is unchanged (`null` effect for level 0).
3. **Reduced-motion behaviour is respected:** when `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is true the effect degrades to a static (non-animated) form; no animation runs in replay/headless mode.
4. **The effect does not depend on, recreate, or conflict with the full-card upgrade border.** It must coexist with the owner-coloured outer border introduced by `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` (owner colour remains the outer border; the shader effect is confined to the upgrade accent), and colour must never be the sole carrier of meaning.
5. **Test/validation criterion:** new unit tests cover the spec builder for base vs upgraded cards (and reduced-motion), plus a browser integration test asserting the effect is attached to an upgraded card and absent on a base card.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (in particular `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § "Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline" and `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No renderer change (fixed):** the game boots with `type: Phaser.CANVAS` (`main.ts`); the effect must work under Canvas. Phaser custom shaders / `postFX` pipelines are WebGL-only and are explicitly **out of scope** for this item.
- **Scope:** only upgraded (level > 0) business / community-space cards. Upgrade-family card faces, events, staff and base cards are out of scope.
- **Coordination with `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`:** that item removes `spec.upgradeBorder` and makes the owner colour the outer card border; this item's effect must sit inside/alongside that (upgrade accent / level badge), never as a full-card stroke.
- Upgraded-card textures are cached once per base card (one texture key per base card, plus a display-name variant); the effect must not multiply texture-cache keys per level.
- Presentation-only: the effect must never mutate game state, transcript, or replay output, and must be skipped in replay/headless mode.
- Reuse the existing overlay pipeline (`src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` + `MainStreetRenderer.applyUpgradeOverlays()`); do not re-rasterise the card SVG on every state change.
- Accessibility: must honour the existing reduced-motion setting (`settingsPanel.reducedMotion`).
- Keep the existing level badge and stat overlays readable and un-occluded; the 64×64 left-art zone and right-hand text column layout (`CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`) must be preserved.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — pure spec builder for upgraded cards: `levelBadge`, `cashLine`, `reputationText`, `upgradeBorder` (flat golden `0xffaa22`, 3 px). This is the natural extension point; note `upgradeBorder` is slated for removal by `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays()` creates the Phaser rectangle/text objects from the spec.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — SVG card faces; upgraded name baked into a display-name variant texture (`CG-0MT24MHGZ0025O20`).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — rasterises SVG → texture (one key per base card; DPR-aware).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimator*` — existing upgrade level-up burst (`animateLevelUp`) and reduced-motion handling; precedent for presentation-only, replay-safe effects.
- `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymGraphicsShaderSpikeScene.ts` — an isolated spike that evaluates sprite tinting and blend modes (NORMAL/ADD/MULTIPLY/SCREEN). It documents shader *feasibility* but does **not** implement a custom fragment shader; it runs under `Phaser.CANVAS`.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § "Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline" documents the current overlay architecture and explicitly rejects per-level SVG variants.
- `main.ts` / `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — both pin `type: Phaser.CANVAS`.
- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` — seat colours / owner-coloured card borders; removes the full-card upgrade border.

## Desired change

Extend `UpgradeOverlaySpec` with a shader-style effect spec (e.g. animated gradient/shimmer accent) and render it with Phaser `Graphics` + tweens in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`. No renderer change; works under Canvas; reduced-motion → static gradient. Base cards unchanged; presentation-only; the pure spec builder remains unit-testable. The effect replaces the *upgrade indicator role* of the removed full-card border without reintroducing a full-card stroke, and coexists with owner-coloured outer borders.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — add the effect spec (colour stops, animation params, reduced-motion static form); reconcile with `upgradeBorder` removal.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — render the effect in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`; add cleanup/tween lifecycle; reconcile with owner-coloured border.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — extend the renderer interface if the effect needs a new method.
- `tests/main-street/UpgradeOverlaySpec.test.ts` — unit tests for the effect spec (base vs upgraded, reduced-motion).
- `tests/main-street/*.browser.test.ts` — browser integration test asserting the effect is present on an upgraded card and absent on a base card.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — update the "Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline" section.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the effect, triggers, and reduced-motion behaviour.

## Related work

Manually identified:

- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` — Identify different AI players (open, intake_complete) — **owns the owner-coloured outer card border and removes the full-card upgrade border**; this item's effect must integrate with it. Both touch `UpgradeOverlaySpec` / `applyUpgradeOverlays`, so sequence or coordinate to avoid rework.
- `MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4` — Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge cards) (open) — adjacent card-face visual change; coordinate so the shader and synergy colouring do not clash.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (open) — owns the card-art/texture pipeline this effect must coexist with.
- `MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN` — Synergy tooltip (completed) — prior card visual/overlay work.
- `MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327` — Move level label to left (completed) — prior upgraded-card overlay adjustment.

## Deferred work

- **`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`** — Migrate Main Street renderer from Canvas to WebGL (deferred; prerequisite for GPU shaders) (open, low priority) — created as a separate `discovered-from` item. A true GPU card shader depends on it. **Not a blocker** for this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Renderer risk (resolved):** Option A keeps the Canvas renderer, so no renderer/CI change is required.
- **Coordination risk (`MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`):** both items modify `UpgradeOverlaySpec` / `applyUpgradeOverlays`; if implemented out of order the upgrade border may be added then removed. Mitigation: agree sequencing (owner-border item first is cleanest) and keep this effect to the upgrade accent, not a full-card stroke.
- **Performance risk:** an always-animating effect on every upgraded card could regress frame rate and headless CI. Mitigation: cap animated cards, pause when off-screen/replay, and provide a static form.
- **Accessibility risk:** animation without a reduced-motion fallback. Mitigation: AC3.
- **Testability risk:** Phaser rendering is hard to unit-test. Mitigation: keep the effect as a pure spec (AC2) and assert spec + presence in a browser test (AC5).
- **Visual-conflict risk:** clashes with owner-coloured competitive rendering (`MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`) and future synergy colouring (`MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4`). Mitigation: keep the effect to the border/accent layer, never the sole carrier of meaning, and avoid the outer border band.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "card shader" could expand to all card families, animated backgrounds, foil effects, etc. Mitigation: scope to upgraded (level > 0) business/community-space cards; record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (approach):** What does "card shader" mean for this project, given the game runs under `Phaser.CANVAS` (custom GPU shaders are WebGL-only)? Options: **(A)** a Canvas-compatible shader-style effect using the existing overlay pipeline; **(B)** switch to WebGL and implement a true custom fragment shader; **(C)** bake an SVG filter/gradient into the upgraded card texture. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): Option A** — Canvas-compatible effect now, with a **deferred, low-priority migration to WebGL**. Source: interactive reply. Research: `main.ts` pins `Phaser.CANVAS`; Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 has no WebGPU backend; `GeometryMask` is Canvas-only and used across Main Street + core UI, so the WebGL migration is a substantial separate effort (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`).
- **Q2 (scope):** Which cards should receive the effect? Options: (a) upgraded business/community-space cards only (level > 0); (b) also upgrade-family card faces; (c) all cards. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): (a)** — upgraded business/community-space cards only.
- **Q3 (existing border):** Replace the flat golden `upgradeBorder`, complement it, or restyle it? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09):** the full-card border is **being removed by the player/AI identification work** (`MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF`), which makes the owner colour the outer card border and moves the upgrade indicator to the level badge / corner accent. This item therefore adds the upgrade shader accent and must not depend on/recreate the full-card border.
- **Q4 (motion):** Static or animated? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): as recommended** — animated, with a reduced-motion static fallback (AC3).
- **Q5 (performance):** Explicit performance/device budget? — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-09): default accepted** — no regression to the existing suite; animation paused in replay/headless.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-10-09):** The current upgrade distinction is a flat golden border + `Lvl N` badge + baked display name, built by the pure `UpgradeOverlaySpec` and rendered by `applyUpgradeOverlays()` (`src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`). The game boots with `type: Phaser.CANVAS` (`main.ts`, `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`), and the engine documents Canvas as a deliberate CI-performance choice (`core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts`). The gym "Shader & Blend Spike" only exercises tint/blend modes — it does not implement a custom fragment shader. Therefore Option A (Canvas-compatible effect) is the feasible path now, with a true GPU shader deferred behind the WebGL migration (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`). `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` will remove the full-card upgrade border, so the upgrade distinction must move to the level badge / corner accent this effect targets.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUWKG6NS006OG2D** – Community Garden should be Entertainment (completed)
- **MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N** – Support arbitrary callback conditions/successors in storyline options (completed)
- **MS-0MUQUBJQF009PTZ0** – Re-tune compensating balance levers (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mt24mhgz0025o20, 0mtorj5fs006b0un, 0xffaa22, absent, ac5 (+387 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, accepted, accessibility, add (+299 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: absent, ac2, ac3, acceptance, accepted (+259 more)

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source)

**Related:** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` (Make card packs available in the browser
distribution — introduces the pack-source registry this builds on)
**Related:** `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (Make card-pack assets self-contained)

## Summary

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, once `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` lands, a bundled
build-time registry. This item adds a **remote pack source** so a pack catalogue
can be hosted at a URL and fetched at runtime — enabling packs to be published
or updated without rebuilding or re-releasing the game.

This is the future-work half of the source-registry design: the registry seam
(`PackSource[]`) is introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`, and this item
implements the remote provider on top of it.

## Goal (user story)

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack (and its catalogue) at
> a URL, so I can publish or update packs for an installed game without
> rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want a remote pack to appear in the Card Packs panel and
> behave exactly like a bundled or content-directory pack (lock → purchase →
> enable → deal), while the game still boots and plays offline on its bundled
> packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` that fetches a pack
   manifest from a configured URL (via the loader's existing `fetchManifest` /
   `fetchCsv` transports) and contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Define how remote source URLs are declared — a build-time
   config constant, a launcher-provided setting, or a well-known manifest URL —
   and how multiple remote sources compose with bundled/static ones.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Define ordering and conflict handling when the same
   pack id appears in more than one source (bundled wins? first wins? reject
   duplicates?). The core merge contract already rejects duplicate card ids
   whole; pack-id precedence must be decided explicitly.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Decide whether remote
   packs may be ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable or serving a
   malformed manifest must degrade to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never block boot, never blank the listing. Define a timeout.
6. **Trust and integrity.** Address the supply-chain surface: remote packs
   inject card rows into the pool, and the merge contract validates the header
   and duplicate ids but not malicious content. Define an integrity mechanism
   (signing, checksum pinning, allow-listed host/ids) and what the game does
   when verification fails.
7. **Caching / offline.** Decide whether remote packs are cached (for example in
   `localStorage` / Cache Storage) so a previously fetched pack remains usable
   offline, and how cache invalidation/versioning works.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, degradation, gating and
   integrity with tests, and document the remote-hosting contract.

## Acceptance criteria (to be confirmed at intake)

1. A pack catalogue hosted at a configured URL is discovered at runtime and its
   packs appear in the Card Packs panel.
2. Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across lock → purchase →
   enable → deal, and save/load.
3. With the remote host unreachable/slow, the game boots on bundled packs and
   warns; the listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad header/duplicate id is
   rejected whole with a warning, without affecting other sources.
5. Pack-id precedence across sources is deterministic and documented.
6. The integrity mechanism rejects a tampered/unverified remote pack and
   documents the failure mode.
7. Remote pack art resolves and renders (coordinated with
   `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`).
8. Documentation covers configuration, the hosting contract, integrity and
   degradation.
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline (a natural follow-up).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; without integrity
  checks a hostile pack could inject arbitrary card data. Mitigation: signing /
  checksum pinning / host allow-list, with a safe refusal mode.
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the game.
  Mitigation: bounded timeout, non-blocking discovery, bundled-first.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack may lose
  it offline. Mitigation: explicit caching decision.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than re-architecting.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source registration and merge ordering.

# Verification: browser pack unlock flow

**Parent:** MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD (Make card packs available in the browser distribution)

## Summary

End-to-end browser verification of the lock → purchase → enable → deal path in the web build, plus Electron parity and save/load degradation regression coverage.

## Scope

- Verification child: owns the browser end-to-end and regression tests, not the production implementation.
- Exercises the real Main Street scene in headless Chromium with no Electron bridges, then exercises the Electron content-directory path.

## Verification approach

- Extend `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackPurchase.browser.test.ts` (or add a focused browser suite) to boot with no `window.tce` bridges and assert the panel lists the residential pack gated with `[ Purchase ]`.
- Drive the scoped simulated purchase, assert the row becomes unlocked / `[ Enable ]`, enable it, and assert a pack card deals in play.
- Reload the page and assert the unlock (and the enabled-pack preference) persist.
- Assert the itch.io golf reward stays locked (no collateral unlock).
- Add Electron-path regression coverage: with `window.tce.contentDir` set, discovery still reads the content directory through `tce-packs://` and the install path is unchanged.
- Add focused save/load and missing/disabled-pack degradation regression tests for the browser path.

## Key Files:

- `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackPurchase.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/CardPackListing.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetPackPurchase.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/helpers/residentialPack.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- In the browser build (no `window.tce.contentDir` and no Electron bridges), Main Street boot discovers the bundled pack so the Card Packs panel lists the residential pack instead of "No card packs installed".
- A **scoped simulated purchase** (declared rule `main-street-residential-pack-purchase`) flips the pack to unlocked and to `[ Enable ]`; enabling it merges its rows so its cards deal in play. A test covers the lock → purchase → enable → deal path in the browser source.
- The simulated purchase is **rule-scoped**: it does not collateral-unlock any other configured reward (for example the itch.io golf reward).
- Browser content-unlock state **persists across a page reload** through the `localStorage`-backed client, and the existing enabled-pack preference continues to persist.
- **Electron behaviour is unchanged**: with `window.tce.contentDir` set, discovery still reads the content directory through the existing `tce-packs://` protocol, and the content-directory install path remains supported.
- Save/load and missing/disabled-pack degradation continue to behave as they do under Electron, covered by focused browser-path regression tests.

# Render the static shader accent

**Parent:** MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38 — Create a card shader
**Slice:** 2 of 4 (rendering layer, test-first)
**Depends on:** Pure upgrade shader-effect spec (slice 1)

## Summary

Render the `shaderEffect` produced by slice 1 through the existing overlay
pipeline. `applyUpgradeOverlays()` draws the effect as a Canvas-safe Phaser
`Graphics`/rectangle accent confined to the top-left upgrade-accent region
(the static / reduced-motion form). Base cards render exactly as today, there
is **no** change to the `Phaser.CANVAS` render type, and the effect coexists
with the owner-coloured outer border without recreating a full-card stroke.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `applyUpgradeOverlays()` renders the `shaderEffect` on upgraded business and community-space cards and renders nothing additional for base cards.
- The static accent is confined to the upgrade accent region (top-left accent / inner glow) and never forms a full-card stroke, so it coexists with the owner-coloured outer card border.
- Upgrade state remains conveyed by the level badge and the accent shape, so colour is never the sole carrier of meaning (accessibility).
- Rendering uses the existing overlay pipeline only: no renderer-type change, no `main.ts` change, and no new texture-cache keys per level.
- A browser integration test asserts the effect object is attached to an upgraded card and absent on a base card.
- The 64x64 left-art zone and right-hand text column layout are preserved; the level badge and stat overlays remain readable and un-occluded.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `applyUpgradeOverlays()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`), when `spec.shaderEffect` is present, create a Phaser `Graphics` (or rectangle) child of the card container drawing the gradient accent in its static form, named for test discovery (e.g. `ms-upgrade-shader`).
- Keep the draw region inside the accent bounds used by `levelAccent`; draw before the level badge so the badge text stays on top.
- Guard on `spec.shaderEffect === null` so base cards are untouched.
- Add the browser integration test (`tests/main-street/*.browser.test.ts`) asserting presence on an upgraded card and absence on a base card via the named game object.

## Deliverables

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — static effect rendering in `applyUpgradeOverlays()` with cleanup-safe creation.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — only if a new helper method is needed (prefer none).
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — presence/absence browser integration test.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — render the static shader accent in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — renderer interface (extend only if required).
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — browser integration assertions.

# Animate the accent with reduced-motion and replay fallback

**Parent:** MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38 — Create a card shader
**Slice:** 3 of 4 (motion layer, test-first)
**Depends on:** Render the static shader accent (slice 2)

## Summary

Animate the shader-style upgrade accent (gradient shimmer sweep) with a Phaser
tween when motion is allowed, and render the static form otherwise. Animation is
gated by `!settingsPanel.reducedMotion && !scene.replayMode`; tweens are cleaned
up on refresh/destroy; the effect is presentation-only and deterministic (no
RNG), following the existing `animateLevelUp` precedent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is `false` and the scene is not in replay/headless mode, the upgrade accent animates via a Phaser tween (gradient/shimmer on the corner accent).
- When `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is `true` the effect renders in its static form and no tween is created.
- No animation is created in replay/headless mode (`scene.replayMode`), so transcripts, replays, and headless CI output are unchanged.
- Tweens and effect game objects are cleaned up when the card container is refreshed or destroyed; no tween/object leak and no measurable regression to the existing suite.
- Unit and/or browser tests verify the animated-vs-static gating (reduced motion on/off) and that the effect never mutates game state, transcript, or replay output.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `applyUpgradeOverlays()`, read `renderer.scene.settingsPanel?.reducedMotion === true` and `renderer.scene.replayMode`; create the tween only when both allow motion.
- Animate a deterministic shimmer (fixed from/to values, no RNG) on the effect graphics; keep the static fill as the reduced-motion/replay form.
- Register the tween/object for cleanup so refreshes do not accumulate tweens; destroy on container removal.
- Extend the slice-2 browser test with reduced-motion on/off cases and add unit coverage for the motion-gating predicate in the pure spec.

## Deliverables

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — animated effect + reduced-motion/replay gating + tween lifecycle cleanup.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — animated vs static and reduced-motion assertions.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — motion-gating spec assertions.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — animation gating and tween lifecycle in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` — reduced-motion/replay browser assertions.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — pure-spec motion-gating tests.
